newsitem.title: INDIA: James Capel's Mohta's reaction to Indian flux.
newsitem.headline: James Capel's Mohta's reaction to Indian flux.

text.p: Sanjeev Mohta, head of research James Capel B & K brokerage in Bombay, on Saturday gave Reuters the following view on Indian markets after the United Front alliance was defeated in a confidence motion and a search for a new coalition got underway.

" I think the Indian economy is in the process of getting depoliticised. The major event that we are looking at is the budget. At the moment, it's not clear what is going to happen on that front. But if it is passed in full or without any major changes, it will be very positive for the economy and it will not really matter who is in power."
"There had been strong hopes that the budget will boost demand, in turn leading to a pick-up in economic activity. This is now going to be delayed."
POLITICAL RISKS TO RISE AFTER RECENT FALL

"As far as the political risk premia goes, I think it actually came down a bit in the last few months. I mean if you look back, no-one gave the United Front government more than six months at the most when it was formed and it lasted ten months.

"I think the political risk premia actually came down and when the budget was announced, there was a favourable reaction. I suppose what will happen is the political risk factor will go back to earlier levels now."

"What is more important is the economic risk premia. Investors have to be convinced that the reforms programme is not going to be affected and that is why the passing of the budget without major changes becomes important. This will convey a clear and positive signal to investors."

DIVESTMENT, FOREIGN INVESTMENT DELAYED "We can't be sure how long the uncertainty wilL last. It may be a couple of days or longer but I personally don't give it beyond three months. Everything should be clear by then."

"Otherwise, obviously there will be a postponement. Divestments will not take place without a government..I think there will also be some holding back of foreign investments until the political situation crystallises."
